g.text: Now AGV-1 heads west instead: π₁ = W18 W22 W41 W41. No dot is shared at any step, yet the lines form

g.text: an X between t = 1 and t = 2: AGV-1 drives W22 → W41 while AGV-2 drives W41 → W22, head-on on the

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: same road. In symbols: π₁(1) = π₂(2) and π₂(1) = π₁(2).

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Fix: one AGV must step aside. AGV-1 pulls into W25, lets AGV-2 pass, then continues: π₁ = W18 W22

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Why the second check is needed: in the time-expanded graph the two swapping AGVs use two different arrows, (W22, 1) → (W41, 2) and (W41, 1) → (W22, 2), so 'no shared dot' and even 'no shared arrow' both pass. What

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: they share is the road W22 – W41 of the garage, in opposite directions during one step. A MAPF solver therefore checks two things: dots (vertex conflicts) and crossing pairs of arrows on the same road (swap conflicts).

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
